== QUEUE RULES == File path: queues/QueueApiName.queue metadataType: Queue memberName: QueueApiName
CRITICAL — ELEMENT ORDER (Salesforce rejects wrong order): <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <Queue xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <doesIncludeBosses>false</doesIncludeBosses> <doesSendEmailToMembers>false</doesSendEmailToMembers> <!-- email: include ONLY when explicitly provided --> <email>queue@example.com</email> <name>Queue Display Name</name> <queueMembers> <!-- see QUEUE MEMBER STRUCTURE below --> </queueMembers> <queueRoutingConfig>RoutingConfigApiName</queueRoutingConfig> <queueSobject> <sobjectType>Case</sobjectType> </queueSobject> </Queue>
MANDATORY ELEMENT ORDER: 1. doesIncludeBosses ("Grant Access Using Hierarchies" in Setup UI — see rule below, this is REQUIRED on every create/update, never omit it) 2. doesSendEmailToMembers 3. email (optional — omit entirely if not provided) 4. name 5. queueMembers (optional — omit entirely if no members) 6. queueRoutingConfig (optional — omit entirely if not provided) 7. queueSobject (one block per object — at least one required)
CRITICAL — NOT EVERY OBJECT SUPPORTS QUEUE OWNERSHIP: Not every standard object can be a Supported Object on a Queue — e.g. Opportunity does NOT support Queues (there is no such thing as an "Opportunity queue" in Salesforce). Before generating any <queueSobject> block, check EVERY object the ticket lists against orgState.existingQueueSupportedObjects — this is the org's real, live list of objects that support Queue ownership (Case, Lead, Task, and most custom __c objects are typically on it; many standard objects, including Opportunity, Account, Contact, are NOT). - If an object IS in that list, generate its <queueSobject> block normally. - If an object is NOT in that list, this is a HARD FAILURE for the entire ticket — do NOT generate any files. Return an error in summary stating plainly, e.g.: "Opportunity does not support Queue ownership in Salesforce — Queues can only be created for Case, Lead, Task, and supported custom objects. This ticket cannot be completed as requested." Do NOT let this surface as Salesforce's raw deploy error ("bad value for restricted picklist field") — catch it here with a clear explanation instead. - If orgState.existingQueueSupportedObjects is entirely absent (older org-state snapshot), fall back to only allowing Case, Lead, Task, and any object ending in __c, and note in summary that the full supported-object list wasn't available to verify against.
CRITICAL — doesIncludeBosses VALUE ("Grant Access Using Hierarchies"): This IS a valid, real Queue element — it is REQUIRED on every generated Queue file, the same way doesSendEmailToMembers is. Never omit it: Salesforce resets an omitted boolean to its default (false) on every deploy, so leaving it out silently UNCHECKS "Grant Access Using Hierarchies" even when the ticket never mentioned it — this has actually happened. Resolve its value the same way as doesSendEmailToMembers: - If the ticket explicitly asks to enable/disable it ("Grant Access Using Hierarchies"), use that value. - Otherwise, for an UPDATE, use the CURRENT value from orgState.existingQueues[].doesIncludeBosses to preserve it exactly as-is. - For a brand-new CREATE with no existingQueues entry and no ticket guidance, default to false.
CRITICAL — queueRoutingConfig VALUE: This must be the routing config's DeveloperName, NOT its display MasterLabel. Match the ticket's routing configuration text against orgState.existingQueueRoutingConfigs by masterLabel, and use that record's developerName as the value — DeveloperNames never contain spaces, so using the label text directly fails deploy with "no QueueRoutingConfig named X found". Generic pattern: masterLabel "Example Routing Config" → developerName "Example_Routing_Config" → <queueRoutingConfig>Example_Routing_Config</queueRoutingConfig>. If no match is found in orgState, do NOT guess a transformed name AND do NOT substitute a DIFFERENT existing routing config from the list just because it's real. Even though queueRoutingConfig is an OPTIONAL element in the Queue schema, if the TICKET explicitly asked for a specific routing configuration, silently omitting it and deploying the rest of the queue anyway means the ticket's explicit request was silently dropped — that is still a failure to do what was asked, even if the deploy itself "succeeds". Treat an unresolvable ticket-requested routing config as a HARD FAILURE for the ENTIRE ticket: → Do NOT generate the Queue file (or any other files in this response) → Return an error in summary explicitly naming the unresolved routing config text and stating no matching Queue Routing Configuration exists in the org — the routing config must be created first, or the ticket corrected, before this can proceed → Do NOT deploy a partial Queue (e.g. one missing only the routing config) and call it done Example: ticket asks for "Support Routing", orgState.existingQueueRoutingConfigs only has "Agent config" and "Skill Bases routing" — neither matches, so NOTHING should be deployed; summary must state "Support Routing" was not found and the ticket cannot be completed as-is.
CRITICAL — UPDATING queueRoutingConfig (or ANY field given as an Existing/Updated pair): When a ticket lists a field as "Existing: X, Updated: Y" (or similarly phrased before/after), the value you deploy MUST be resolved from Y (the Updated/new side), NEVER from X (the Existing/old side) — this applies to every such field, not just queueRoutingConfig. Do not let the old value "win" just because it's also mentioned in the ticket, or because an old value happens to resemble an example shown elsewhere in this prompt — always re-derive the NEW value's resolution independently. Worked example: Ticket: "Routing Configuration: Existing = Example Routing Config, Updated = Other Routing Config" orgState.existingQueueRoutingConfigs contains both masterLabels. WRONG: <queueRoutingConfig>Example_Routing_Config</queueRoutingConfig> (this is the OLD value — do not deploy this) CORRECT: <queueRoutingConfig>Other_Routing_Config</queueRoutingConfig> (resolved from the Updated value)
CRITICAL — QUEUE MEMBER STRUCTURE: There are FIVE distinct member-type wrappers. EACH wrapper appears AT MOST ONCE inside <queueMembers>, holding MULTIPLE inner elements for multiple members of that type — NEVER repeat the same wrapper tag. Salesforce rejects a repeated wrapper with: "Element roles is duplicated at this location in type QueueMembers" (or users/publicGroups/etc).
<queueMembers> <users> <user>alice@company.com</user> <user>bob@company.com</user> </users> <publicGroups> <publicGroup>Sales_Team</publicGroup> </publicGroups> <roles> <role>Customer_Support_International</role> </roles> <roleAndSubordinates> <roleAndSubordinate>Some_Role_External_Inclusive</roleAndSubordinate> </roleAndSubordinates> <roleAndSubordinatesInternal> <roleAndSubordinateInternal>SVP_Customer_Service_Support</roleAndSubordinateInternal> </roleAndSubordinatesInternal> </queueMembers>
MEMBER TYPE MEANINGS — pick the wrapper matching what the ticket actually asks for: - "Users" / named individuals → <users><user>...</user></users> - "Public Groups" → <publicGroups><publicGroup>...</publicGroup></publicGroups> - "Roles" (role only, no subordinates) → <roles><role>...</role></roles> - "Roles and Subordinates" (includes portal/external users in the hierarchy) → <roleAndSubordinates><roleAndSubordinate>...</roleAndSubordinate></roleAndSubordinates> - "Roles and Internal Subordinates" (includes subordinates, INTERNAL users only — the common case; this is what most tickets mean by "role hierarchy") → <roleAndSubordinatesInternal><roleAndSubordinateInternal>...</roleAndSubordinateInternal></roleAndSubordinatesInternal> "Roles" and "Roles and Internal Subordinates" are DIFFERENT wrappers even when the ticket lists them near each other — never fold a "Roles and Internal Subordinates" entry into <roles>.
RESOLVING DISPLAY NAMES TO REAL IDENTIFIERS: - Roles: match the ticket's role text (e.g. "Customer Support, International") against orgState.existingRoles by Name — a comma is very often PART of a real Salesforce role Name (e.g. "Customer Support, EMEA" is one role, not two), so do NOT split it. Use that role's developerName as the value. If no match is found in orgState, do NOT guess a transformed name — return an error in summary listing the unresolved role text instead. - Users: match the ticket's person name (e.g. "Mahesh Pawar") against orgState.existingUsers by Name and use that user's username as the value inside <user>. If no match is found, do NOT guess an email address — return an error in summary listing the unresolved name. - Public Groups: match against orgState.existingGroups by name/developerName the same way. - If orgState.existingRoles or existingUsers is entirely absent (older org-state snapshot), fall back to omitting that member type and stating in summary which names could not be resolved — never fabricate a DeveloperName or username.
OTHER RULES: - <name> is the display label - Queue API name (DeveloperName) has no spaces — use underscores - The Queue metadata type has NO description field at all — the "Queue Description" box visible in Setup UI does not map to anything deployable via Metadata API. If a ticket provides a description, do NOT invent an element for it and do NOT silently drop it — generate the rest of the Queue normally, but the ticket summary MUST explicitly state: "Description could not be set — the Queue metadata type has no description field (this is a Salesforce platform limitation, not a pipeline gap)." - For UPDATE: existingQueues gives you email, doesSendEmailToMembers, doesIncludeBosses, sobjectTypes, and members — preserve those unless the ticket changes them. doesIncludeBosses in particular is REQUIRED on the regenerated file even when the ticket says nothing about it — omitting it resets "Grant Access Using Hierarchies" to unchecked. queueRoutingConfig is NOT part of existingQueues (Salesforce doesn't expose that association via the same query) — it lives ONLY in the separate existingQueueRoutingConfigs list. Do NOT treat "not present in existingQueues" as "this queue has no routing config to update" — that field is simply tracked elsewhere. If the ticket mentions a routing configuration change (old or new value), you MUST include <queueRoutingConfig> in the regenerated XML, resolved via existingQueueRoutingConfigs exactly as described above — never silently omit it because it wasn't part of the existingQueues bundle you started from. - For DELETE: Use destructiveFiles with metadataType Queue and member = Queue API name
